archetypes.name: exit-contract
archetypes.rationale: close_sources_main returns exit-code 1 on any skip or warning, which may abort skill-script callers under set -e; prose_audit_main hard-fails on any single comment-read error mid-scan; JSON-status vs exit-code contracts differ across list_open_main, prose_audit_main, and close_sources_main.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect the exit-code contract of every new CLI verb added to python/combine_issues.py, especially close_sources_main (which returns 1 when any source is skipped, even legitimately), prose_audit_main (which aborts the entire audit on a single comment-read failure via `return _emit_json(...) or 1`), and list_open_main (which emits JSON before returning 1). Check whether the oos-7 step in .claude/skills/combine-issues/SKILL.md, or any Bash caller running under set -e, will silently abort after a partial-success close-sources call and skip the oos-10 summary. Verify that every hard-stop path in the skill emits a diagnostic before stopping so that deferred-but-unclosed sources are not silently lost. Check whether the inconsistency between exit-code and JSON-status across the new verbs would cause the skill to reach inconsistent intermediate state in error paths. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: code-reuse
archetypes.rationale: _CODE_FENCE_RE, _MARKDOWN_PREFIX_RE, _EXAMPLE_PREFIX_RE, and _NEGATION_RE are defined identically in both blocker.py and combine_issues.py; _parse_prose_blocks in combine_issues.py also reimplements logic nearly identical to blocker.parse_prose_blockers.
archetypes.prompt_body: The four regex constants _CODE_FENCE_RE, _MARKDOWN_PREFIX_RE, _EXAMPLE_PREFIX_RE, and _NEGATION_RE appear identically in python/blocker.py and python/combine_issues.py, and the prose-parsing function _parse_prose_blocks in combine_issues.py closely mirrors parse_prose_blockers from blocker.py (differing mainly in which keyword direction it matches). Assess the maintenance risk created by this duplication: if one copy diverges (e.g., a future tweak to negation detection in blocker.py), the combine_issues.py copy will silently behave differently. Determine whether combine_issues.py should import the shared constants and/or delegate to parse_prose_blockers from blocker instead of reimplementing, noting whether the directional asymmetry between the two functions is a genuine reason to keep them separate. Also check whether the `_parse_prose_blocks` negation check (applied to the entire pre-# prefix) and the `parse_prose_blockers` negation check (applied only to the prefix before the match start) are semantically equivalent or subtly different in a way that matters for real issue bodies. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
